The idea behind presuppositionless philosophy is that our assumptions about the world can limit our understanding and prevent us from gaining truly objective knowledge.

This approach is often contrasted with more traditional philosophical methods, which rely on pre-existing beliefs and assumptions about the world, such as metaphysical or ontological claims.
